# `source_flow`

the flow of the cortical current per atom of the joint frequency x cortical eigenvalue level - a minimum-norm kernel projected onto the cortex's eigenmodes (options A and B, per hemisphere or glued), power, phase currents, Hodge-Dirac flow, band pairs, time cells and their sign-flip test.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run source_flow --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run source_flow --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run source_flow --dataset D --subject S --recording REC --all --kernel KERNEL --cortex per_hemisphere --left LEFT --right RIGHT --columns channels --atoms ATOMS --bands BANDS
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `recording` | field recording, each true, where {"name": "$recording"} | yes |
| `kernel` | operator inverse kernel, from recording.manifold.0, where {"name": "$kernel"} (a free-orientation minimum-norm kernel (`nxr-neuro run inverse` first)) | yes |
| `left` | operator eigenvectors, where {"name": "${left}_eigenvectors"}, when {"cortex": "per_hemisphere"} (the left hemisphere's Hodge-Dirac solve (`nxr-neuro run eigenmodes --surface <left hemisphere>`)) | yes |
| `right` | operator eigenvectors, where {"name": "${right}_eigenvectors"}, when {"cortex": "per_hemisphere"} (the right hemisphere's Hodge-Dirac solve) | yes |
| `glued` | operator eigenvectors, where {"name": "${glued}_eigenvectors"}, when {"cortex": "glued"} (the glued cortex's Hodge-Dirac solve (`nxr-neuro run glue`, then `eigenmodes`)) | yes |
| `sensor_package` | operator eigenvectors, where {"name": "${sensor_package}_eigenvectors"}, when {"columns": "sensor_coordinates"} (the sensor surface's Hodge-Dirac solve (option A)) | yes |
| `channel_map` | field any, where {"name": "$channel_map"}, when {"columns": "sensor_coordinates"} (the sensor surface's vertex-to-channel map (option A)) | yes |
| `atoms` | selection any, where {"name": "$atoms"} (the frequency atoms, a kernel set (`nxr-neuro run select_kernels --profile gaussian --chart linear --width-rule proportional` first)) | yes |
| `pairs` | selection any, where {"name": "$pairs"} (the band pairs' members: atoms x bands x bands (`nxr-neuro run select_kernel_product --factors 3 --first ATOMS --second BANDS --third BANDS` first)) | yes |
| `atom_bands` | selection any, where {"name": "$atom_bands"} (the sign-flip test's members per band: atoms x bands (`nxr-neuro run select_kernel_product --factors 2` first)) | yes |
| `bands` | selection any, where {"name": "$bands"} (the cortical eigenvalue bands, a kernel set (`nxr-neuro run select_kernels --profile cos2_partition`; centres as wavelengths in the surface's unit)) | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pairs` | `--pairs` | none | - |  | the product atoms x bands x bands by name: the band pairs are measured over its members |
| `atom_bands` | `--atom-bands` | none | - |  | the product atoms x bands by name: the sign-flip test per band is measured over its members (the whole field's over the atoms) |
| `recording` | `--recording` | `none` | - |  | the recording's name, or none: every recording of the subject, one run each |
| `kernel` | `--kernel` | none | - |  | the free-orientation minimum-norm kernel's name (the caller's: the reference used one made with the empty-room noise covariance and the cardiac and blink projectors kept) |
| `cortex` | `--cortex` | `per_hemisphere` | - | per_hemisphere, glued | per_hemisphere (each hemisphere with its own modes: the reference's, so the default by the method rule) \| glued (one solve on the glued cortex: the kernel's rows selected, the bridge zero, the medial wall dropped); both are named options, to compare |
| `left` | `--left` | none | - |  | per_hemisphere: the left hemisphere's Hodge-Dirac solve's stem |
| `right` | `--right` | none | - |  | per_hemisphere: the right hemisphere's Hodge-Dirac solve's stem |
| `glued` | `--glued` | none | - |  | glued: the glued cortex's Hodge-Dirac solve's stem |
| `columns` | `--columns` | `channels` | - | sensor_coordinates, channels | channels (option B: the operator acts on the channels, as the reference's kernel does, so the default by the method rule) \| sensor_coordinates (option A: it acts on the served sensor field coordinates; what the sensor solve leaves out is stated); both are named options, to compare |
| `sensor_package` | `--sensor-package` | none | - |  | option A: the sensor surface's Hodge-Dirac solve's stem |
| `channel_map` | `--channel-map` | none | - |  | option A: the sensor surface's vertex-to-channel map's name |
| `atoms` | `--atoms` | none | - |  | the frequency atoms' kernel set by name |
| `bands` | `--bands` | none | - |  | the cortical eigenvalue bands' kernel set by name (the last member is the complement) |
| `overlap_samples` | `--overlap-samples` | `16384` | samples |  | the overlap on each side of a chunk: half a chunk, as sensor_flow |
| `transform_samples` | `--transform-samples` | `65536` | samples |  | each chunk's one transform: the chunk and its two overlaps, as sensor_flow |
| `frequency_span` | `--frequency-span` | `[0, 60]` | Hz |  | [lo, hi) the bins kept of each chunk's transform (the physiological bands) |
| `frequency_normalisation` | `--frequency-normalisation` | `sum_of_squared_gains` | - | sum_of_squared_gains, none | the atoms divided at each bin by the square root of their squared gains' sum \| none, as sensor_flow |
| `support_floor` | `--support-floor` | `0.001` | - |  | a bin whose atoms' squared gains sum to less than this fraction of their largest sum lies outside the atoms (gain 0) |
| `time_cells` | `--time-cells` | true | - |  | also read each atom's time cells on the cortex and test them (sign flip): a GEMM per cell of 3 x vertices x the columns x the cell's samples, about 0.5 T multiply-adds per chunk, atom and band on a 20 000-vertex cortex (a GPU's work) |
| `cell_width` | `--cell-width` | `2.0` | - |  | a time cell's width in the atom's time standard deviations, snapped to the nearest power of two of samples |
| `flip_elements` | `--flip-elements` | `edges` | - | edges, vertices | the sign-flip test's elements: edges \| vertices |
| `patterns` | `--patterns` | `2000` | - |  | the sign-flip test's random patterns |
| `seed` | `--seed` | `0` | - |  | the seed of numpy's default_rng for the sign patterns |
| `cells_per_flip` | `--cells-per-flip` | `1` | cells |  | consecutive time cells one sign flips together (the measured correlation of neighbouring cells is stored with the result as the check) |
| `name` | `--name` | `{recording}_{kernel}` | - |  | the stem of the stored names |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE SOURCE MAPPING OF THE SENSOR-SPACE FLOW (spec docs/specs/2026-11-24-source-flow.md): the flow of the cortical current estimate per atom of the joint frequency x cortical eigenvalue
level. The source step is an existing minimum-norm kernel PROJECTED ONTO THE CORTEX'S EIGENMODES, nothing else: no inverse is derived here, no prior over modes is added; the kernel is
the caller's named input.

THE GRAPH. before: the cortex's Hodge-Dirac eigenvectors (per hemisphere, or the glued cortex) + the kernel --[signal.mode_analysis, exact_and_constant, unit_mass]--> the kernel in the
cortex's mode coordinates, each Cartesian component (no orientation assumed; a hemisphere's rows or the glued cortex's kept rows SELECTED, the bridge zero) --[signal.source_mode_operator]-->
option A (columns sensor_coordinates: composed with the sensor surface's field coordinates' synthesis, acting on the served chunk spectra) or option B (columns channels: acting on the
channels), with the kernel's rows in the same columns and the serving operator of the spectra.
chunks: as `sensor_flow`: each chunk with an overlap of half a chunk on each side --[signal.overlapped_spectrum]--> --[signal.chunk_spectra]--> the cross-spectrum in its factored form
(in sensor field coordinates for option A, in channels for option B).
after: --[signal.cortical_flow: the atoms x the cortical cos² bands (the last the complement: the kernel minus every other band) and their pairs]--> power, phase current per edge and per
vertex, Hodge-Dirac flow coefficients on the cortex's stored edge rows, potential and stream, and the remainder beyond the kept modes (split by sparse Poisson solves); per hemisphere
or glued; --[signal.cortical_time_cells]--> the same per time cell of each atom, for the whole field and each band; --[stats.sign_flip_consistency]--> R1 per edge.
Every value below is a stated choice of this definition or the caller's (the nodes default nothing).

What it cannot resolve: the same estimate as the kernel, in other coordinates (its point spread, depth bias and field spread are inherited; flow at cortical wavelengths the kernel
cannot resolve is leakage, not travel); rank at most the sensor coordinates (option A) or the kernel's; wavelengths shorter than the last kept mode only in the complement band;
per hemisphere: no flow across the midline; glued: no medial-wall sources; the apparent speed derived at read is an upper bound.

  nxr-neuro run source_flow --dataset D --subject S --recording REC --all --kernel KERNEL --cortex per_hemisphere --left LEFT --right RIGHT --columns channels --atoms ATOMS --bands BANDS
```
